title: Elysian Bio - POC scoping: open models & benchmarks
summary: POC scoping call to agree success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and shortlist open-models for a 4-week POC. Key concerns: domain accuracy on biomedical literature, hallucination rate, data residency/IP protection, latency & cost tradeoffs. Agreed: evaluation dataset (500 queries), two-week pilot baseline + 4-week full POC, initial shortlist: Mistral-instruct, Falcon-40B, Llama-2-70B (quant/pt), and Red-verified distilled variant. Next steps: Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet, security docs, and cost estimates; customer to share eval set and sample queries.
topics: Workload sizing (QPS, concurrency, tokens per request)

SE to run initial latency/cost estimates for shortlisted models by 2026-12-07

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-02 15:00 PST | Duration 52m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (Elysian Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Platform), Aisha Rahman (PM)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we all have the agenda--quick intros then dive into success criteria and model shortlist.
[00:14] Priya Nair: thanks Maya, yeah quick background — Elysian does literature curation and signal extraction from papers and patents, lots of biomedical terminology, we care a lot about precision and hallucination rates, also some multi-lingual (english + simplified mandarin) for our APAC ingestion.
[00:35] Owen Patel: cool, that helps. can you share rough numbers for throughput and request shape? tokens per request, avg and p95?
[00:45] Samir Gupta: sure, typical request is 400-800 tokens in, we generate 200-600 tokens out for long summaries, peak QPS is currently around 6-8 qps but we expect burst to 25 qps across two regions. concurrency around 40 concurrent streams during peak.
[01:05] Lena Ortiz: and what's success from your POV — latency SLO, accuracy, cost targets?
[01:12] Aisha Rahman: primary metric is domain F1 on our labeled set, target is >= 0.78 on entity extraction and <= 5% hallucination on structured outputs. Latency SLO is <750ms tail for short queries, but for long form summaries we accept 2-3s. Cost-wise we want to keep inference cost under $0.07 per summary on average.
[01:42] Maya Chen: great, that's concrete and very helpful. So we'll propose a two-stage POC: 2-week pilot to validate infra/connectivity and run initial benchmarks, then a 4-week POC to iterate on prompts, quantization, and routing policies.
[01:58] Priya Nair: sounds good. on security, we need IP protections - likely a private deployment or dedicated pools, can't have raw data leave VPC without controls. SOC2 plus audit logs and KMS integration required.
[02:15] Owen Patel: understood — Redwood Private or Dedicated can do VPC peering or private link and KMS/HSM integration. For the POC we usually do a dedicated pool in our managed infra with customer VPC peering, or if you prefer we can run a private control plane. We'll send security pack.
[02:33] Samir Gupta: we prefer dedicated in first phase, less ops on our side. We also need token-level cost visibility.
[02:40] Maya Chen: noted.

[02:55] Maya Chen: model shortlist — we've prepped open models that map to your needs. thinking: Mistral-instruct (good generation quality, smaller compute), Falcon-40B (strong reasoning, but heavier), Llama-2-70B instruct or distilled 30B variant (good multilingual capabilities), and a Redwood-verified distilled variant that trades some quality for cost. Thoughts?
[03:20] Priya Nair: curious about hallucinations — historically we've seen Falcon produce better factuality on biochemical Qs, but Llama variants handle multilingual prompts better. Mistral looks cheap but not tested on our domain.
[03:38] Owen Patel: correct — tradeoffs: Falcon-40B tends to have stronger factual grounding in many bench datasets but is more expensive; Llama-2-70B (quantized) with instruction fine-tuning does well multilingual and can be compressed to 4-bit for cost, but some hallucination risk unless we add retrieval/evidence grounding. Mistral-instruct is often very efficient and good at instruction-following but may need domain-tuning.
[03:58] Lena Ortiz: for structured outputs we recommend adding constrained decoding and schema-checkers plus the Redwood structured-output module — that reduces hallucination in JSON outputs. Also consider hybrid routing: cheap model for drafts, larger model for verification.
[04:18] Aisha Rahman: do you have recommendations for evaluation? we want a reproducible benchmark.
[04:24] Maya Chen: yes — propose: 500 queries representative of your workload: 60% literature summarization, 30% entity extraction, 10% question answering. Metrics: F1 for entities, exact match for structured fields, hallucination rate (manual labels), latency (p50/p95), cost per request. We'll run each model at fixed batch settings and with quantization options.
[04:48] Samir Gupta: what about caching and prefix KV cache — for summaries it won't help much but for repeated Q/A it will. cost estimates should include that.
[04:57] Owen Patel: agreed — we'll simulate your traffic profile including TTL for caching. Redwood runtime supports prefix caching and continuous batching; we can show delta with/without.

[05:10] Priya Nair: multilingual — Chinese support critical for 20% of our pipeline. Which models do best?
[05:18] Owen Patel: Llama-2 variants and some Falcon versions have decent multi-lingual, Mistral less so out-of-box. For production we often do a lightweight language-detection routing, send Chinese content to a model fine-tuned or distilled for mandarin, or add retrieval in Chinese. We can include bilingual eval splits.
[05:36] Maya Chen: we'll include bilingual subset (~100 queries) in eval.

[05:44] Aisha Rahman: timeline — you mentioned 2-week pilot then 4-week POC — can you outline deliverables per phase?
[05:52] Maya Chen: pilot (2 weeks): infra setup (dedicated pool, VPC peering), connectivity test, run baseline benchmarks on 3 models with default prompts, deliver latency/cost report. Full POC (4 weeks): iterate on prompts, apply quantization and potential LORA/fine-tune on small labeled set, run final benchmark, handover runbook, and ops dashboard.
[06:12] Samir Gupta: what's your support SLA during POC?
[06:16] Lena Ortiz: 24x5 for pilot, 24x7 for critical incidents if we agree; SE availability for run debugging. We'll put that in the runbook.

[06:30] Owen Patel: on benchmarking specifics — we'll measure token-level throughput, model latency at p50/p95/p99, memory footprint, and cost per 1k tokens assuming your reserved capacity. For quantization we'll try 4-bit AQT and q8_0 conversions to see quality delta.
[06:50] Priya Nair: fine-tuning — we have approx 2k labeled examples can we do LoRA?
[06:55] Owen Patel: yes LoRA on 7B/30B sized variants works well; for 70B it's heavier but possible with parameter efficient fine-tuning. For POC we suggest LoRA on distilled 30B or Mistral-instruct to see quick gains.

[07:10] Maya Chen: blockers? anything else from legal or compliance?
[07:14] Samir Gupta: we need to review the SOC2 + data residency addendum. Also confirm data retention and audit logs.
[07:21] Maya Chen: we'll send the security pack and the SLA addendum.

[07:30] Priya Nair: on eval labels — hallucination measurement is a little fuzzy, we can provide a rubric. We'll send that.
[07:36] Maya Chen: perfect.

[07:44] Aisha Rahman: curious about cost — can you ballpark cost for each model per summary with our average token counts?
[07:52] Owen Patel: rough back-of-envelope given your 600 tokens in + 300 out average: 
- Mistral-instruct (30B equivalent quantized): $0.03 - $0.05 per summary
- Falcon-40B (fp16): $0.08 - $0.12 per summary
- Llama-2-70B quantized + LoRA: $0.05 - $0.09 per summary
These are rough; we'll produce a more precise table in the benchmark spreadsheet that accounts for batching, caching, and reserved pricing.
[08:38] Priya Nair: those numbers align with our internal targets.

[08:45] Maya Chen: ok recap of next steps — Redwood sends benchmark template + security pack + cost estimate, Elysian shares eval set and QPS matrix, schedule pilot kickoff. Anything to add?
[08:57] Samir Gupta: include example infra diagrams for dedicated pool + VPC peering.
[09:02] Owen Patel: will do, also include example runbook and rollbacks.

[09:10] Priya Nair: thanks everyone, excited to try the models.
[09:14] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll send follow-up email with links — benchmark spreadsheet, security docs, and a calendar invite for kickoff.

[09:22] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels auto-assigned, minor transcription errors (Redwood product names sometimes come out as 'Red wood'), filler words and overlaps present. Shared artifacts referenced: benchmark_spreadsheet.xlsx (link in follow up), redwood-security-pack.pdf (link in follow up), sample prompt set.
